data.narrative:
Anyon Systems is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised C$23M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 11 peers—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private entities including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ—though same-stage comparables within quantum computing remain sparse.

Stage-progression analysis, the applicable triangulation method, uses the C$23M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $46M. A sensitivity band of $39M (low) to $53M (high) reflects reasonable variance around this midpoint estimate, anchored to stage-progression mechanics rather than market multiples.

The peer-median approach is not applicable: while 8 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables yields insufficient datapoints (need ≥3). Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unwarranted noise. The valuation range of $39M–$53M, with a median of $46M, rests on a single method and therefore carries material dependency risk. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-stage peer pricing, near-term financing expectations, and the early-stage variability inherent in quantum computing commercialization timelines. External validation through forward financing rounds or expanded peer data would strengthen conviction in this range.
